hypothesis: The exact CP-SAT DTS formulation is computationally viable when run with OR-Tools 9.12.4544, a runtime that passes the previously crashing control model, and can produce a validator-accepted scope-111 witness or a meaningful solver status.
rationale: The prior CP-SAT experiment was blocked by an OR-Tools 9.15.6755 Windows access violation before any solver status was returned. An isolated alternate wheel passes the same three-variable AllDifferent control, directly changing the environmental condition without changing the frozen DTS model or validator.
expected_information_gain: Separates the prior native-runtime failure from the mathematical/search difficulty of the exact model, yielding either a complete independently checked witness or a time-bounded feasible/unknown status from a functioning exact solver.
method: Run the existing exact integer CP-SAT model with 42 mark variables, 105 exact difference variables, global AllDifferent, strict normalization, scope <=111, and first-mark row symmetry. Use OR-Tools CP-SAT 9.12.4544 from the ignored runtime cache, Python 3.12.10, eight workers, a fixed seed, and independently validate any returned rows with verify_dts.verify.
metric: CP-SAT status, elapsed time, returned rows, and independent DTS validity
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A FEASIBLE or OPTIMAL result accepted by the independent integer validator is exactly a true-objective scope<=111 witness; UNKNOWN or timeout is solver evidence only and not a mathematical infeasibility result.
kill_condition: Stop after 120 seconds or immediately on a complete solution that passes the independent validator; do not interpret UNKNOWN as infeasibility.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: strict improvement only if FEASIBLE and validator-valid

interpretation: Pre-registered runtime-enabled exact DTS test; no candidate claim is made until independent validation.
recommended_next_action: If the alternate runtime returns UNKNOWN, use that result to evaluate a solver/representation change rather than repeating the same model with more wall time; if it returns FEASIBLE, begin adversarial and clean-checkout verification immediately.
repetition_justification: This revisits the exact CP-SAT model only after a materially changed runtime condition: OR-Tools 9.12.4544 passes a control model where 9.15.6755 crashed. It is a capability-isolation test, not a repeat of the blocked run under the same environment.
